sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes several articulated neck vertebrae, parts of the shoulder and back vertebrae, ribs, belly ribs (gastralia), shoulder blades (coracoids and scapulae), and possible fragments of the hip bone (ilium).
Each preserved neck and back vertebra measures roughly 30 cm in length.
From the hip region the trunk is estimated at about 60 cm, while the upper arm bone (humerus) suggests a forelimb length of 60–70 cm.
Overall body length is inferred to have been between 1.5 and 2 m.
The animal likely possessed between 29 and 39 neck vertebrae and 20 to 23 back vertebrae.
Osvaldo Rojas and his team uncovered the fossils in 2014 at the Ojo Opache site, roughly 10 km west of Calama in northern Chile.
The rocks yielding the specimen belong to the Quehuita Formation of Chile.
The extent of vertebral fusion indicates the individual was a subadult approaching full maturity when it died.
Gondwananectes lived in the Middle Jurassic Bajocian age.
Database records place it in the Bajocian stage, about 170.9 to 168.2 million years ago, with a single known occurrence.
Subsequent preparation revealed that bones previously identified as pelvic elements are actually parts of the shoulder girdle.
